Astronaut Dale Gardner, hanging off the Space Shuttle, holds up a "For Sale" sign referring to the 2 spent satellites he just recovered in 2 space walks. 1984

Astronaut Dale A. Gardner, having just completed the major portion of his second extravehicular activity period in three days, holds up a "For Sale" sign referring to the two satellites, Palapa B-2 (Indonesian Telecomm) and Westar 6 (Western Union geosync) that they retrieved from orbit after their Payload Assist Modules (PAM) failed to fire. Astronaut Joseph P. Allen IV, who also participated in the two EVAs, is reflected in Gardner's helmet visor. A portion of each of two recovered satellites is in the lower right corner, with Westar 6 nearer Discovery's aft.

The mission was funded by the insurance companies that insured the launch of those two satellites. The Westar was brought back to earth then resold to AsiaSat in Hong Kong, who refurbished it and relaunched it on April 7, 1990 as AsiaSat 1. The Palapa was physically placed in its proper orbit by the Shuttle.
